# Independent audit: a weighted base center outside every proper face

Audited source: `candidate 9ae432ab1b731d70`, Sections 1–6. Verdict: **PASS**. This is a finite arithmetic statement; it makes no mixed-depth or buffer-continuity assertion.

## Exact hypotheses

Let P be a finite lattice-complete set in an affine lattice, with positive weights of total M and k occupied parity classes. Let F be a proper face of conv(P). A closed minor is T=P intersect conv(T); its lattice is inherited, not reset by a possibly nonsaturated affine reparametrization. The needed hypotheses are only V(T)<=k(T)M/k for the nonempty closed minors contained in F.

For a subset in a lower-dimensional affine span, inherited parity agrees with the restriction of ambient parity: if p−q is twice an ambient lattice vector, its half already lies in the direction space of that affine span. Thus the parity comparison in the source uses exactly the quota's k(T).

## Independent proof check

Set alpha=M/k and assume every outside point has a closed containing cap of mass strictly below alpha. Choose finitely many such caps and increase their complementary open-system thresholds in a compact box, preserving exclusion of all outside points, to maximize their sum.

A nonsaturated threshold has an outside equality witness that strictly satisfies every other inequality. Otherwise it can be increased: the relevant set of outside points is finite, and all their positive gaps have a positive minimum. Saturated inequalities strictly contain every point of P on their open side and are redundant on P.

The surviving open trace T lies in F. Its convex hull remains in the same open convex set, proving that it is a closed minor. The selected equality witnesses have distinct parities: a same-parity midpoint belongs to P, strictly satisfies every inequality, and cannot belong to F because an interior segment point in a face forces both endpoints into that face. The same argument between a witness and a survivor shows that witness parities and T parities are disjoint. Hence r+k(T)<=k.

The r nonsaturated closed caps cover P\T, and each still has mass strictly below alpha. Consequently M−V(T)<r alpha<=(k−k(T))alpha. If T is empty this is M<M. If T is nonempty it contradicts its stated quota. This proves an outside point of base depth at least M/k.

## Boundary and scope checks

All original and expanded bad caps are closed, so equality atoms are counted. The open complements are essential in both midpoint contradictions. No limiting perturbation of weights or normals is used. Positive rank zero has no nonempty proper face; the empty-face version is the usual occupied-parity center theorem. Affine functionals constant on the affine span cannot be selected as light containing caps, so they cause no missing direction case.

The arbitrary-threshold alternative in Section 5 follows from the same strict covering inequality, including an empty surviving trace when tau>M/k. Under the quotas, the base-center set cannot be contained in a proper face. This means its convex hull meets the relative interior; it does not require an interior lattice center.

The theorem is stronger than the earlier sufficient criterion k(P)−k(F)>=Gamma_d k(P\F). The prismatoid example with shared outside parities does not contradict it: the proof counts selected equality-witness parities, not all outside parities.

Geometric-mean affine normalization still requires a separate fixed-epsilon boundary argument. This arithmetic proof supplies no uniform small-buffer bound along epsilon-dependent minimizing multipliers; the exact example in `candidate 7051dc5265e081de` records that distinction.
